A1.justification: Both PDFs describe LeanQuant by the same authors. The complete main texts and appendices, including equations, algorithms, figures and tables, support reliable comparison despite substantial revision and relocation.

before.justification: v1 reports original LeanQuant perplexity, zero-shot accuracy, BERT/SQuAD results, ablations and efficiency measurements in Tables 1–8 and Figure 3.

after.justification: v2 reports original affine and non-uniform quantization results, large-model evaluations, MT-Bench judgments, resource measurements and ablations, alongside retained BERT results.

M1.justification: v1 learns non-uniform grids using k-means++ initialization. v2 adds loss-aware affine-grid optimization over scaling factors and zero-points, with a fused search kernel, and introduces uniformly spaced initialization for non-uniform clustering. Algorithms 1 and 2 now support both grid types.

E1.justification: v2 adds LAMBADA, MMLU, HellaSwag and instruction-following evaluation on MT-Bench, substantially broadening task requirements. WikiText-2, C4, ARC, PIQA, WinoGrande and SQuAD remain; the BERT/SQuAD experiment moves to Appendix A.1.

E2.justification: The zero-shot comparisons drop QUIP and introduce GPTQ and SqueezeLLM while retaining OmniQuant. Grouped GPTQ/AWQ rows disappear from the perplexity comparison, while SqueezeLLM gains C4 comparisons beyond its earlier WikiText-2 evaluation. The OBQ comparison for BERT remains unchanged.

E3.justification: v2 reports p = 4 throughout instead of v1's bit-dependent 2.5/3/3.5 defaults. It adds Llama-3 and Mistral configurations up to 405B, grouped affine evaluations and GPT-4o judging. Quantization measurements use L40s or dual RTX 8000 GPUs instead of V100 hardware. The C4 calibration and perplexity sequence procedures are retained.

E4.justification: v2 adds controlled initialization comparisons in Table 11 and fused-kernel on/off experiments in Table 5. Sensitivity and layerwise loss-error analyses now cover both grid types and additional models. v1's uninformed-grid comparison is retained conceptually through the p = 0 rows in v2 Table 10.

E5.justification: Neither version reports experimental seed values, repeated-run counts, confidence intervals or significance tests. The new MT-Bench win/tie/loss counts and win rates are point results, without an accompanying uncertainty analysis.

E6.justification: v2 adds affine, MT-Bench, 123B/405B and resource results, while removing the decoding-latency results and LLaMA-1-30B/65B entries. Non-uniform 3-bit Llama-2-7B WikiText-2 perplexity changes from 6.30 to 6.19 under revised settings; BERT F1 scores remain identical. New Tables 1/8 contain GPTQ averages excluding ARC-E, and Table 8 repeats several non-uniform result rows across 7B/13B models.

T1.justification: v2 adds formal definitions for uniformly spaced initialization and the constrained affine-grid optimization in Equation 7. The Taylor approximation, OBQ loss-error derivation and Hessian updates remain substantively unchanged. The existing error-accumulation argument moves to Appendix B; no new theorem or proof is added.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion expand the contribution from accurate non-uniform quantization and inference acceleration to compatibility across quantization formats and scalable grid learning. Compatibility with existing inference kernels and quantization up to 405B become central claims.

C2.justification: v2 questions whether perplexity represents downstream accuracy and attributes non-uniform grids' lower loss errors to greater placement freedom. The central outlier-preservation explanation remains. v1's specific limitations concerning truthfulness, fairness, interpretability and adversarial robustness are removed.

D1.justification: v2 documents the affine search granularity, GPU thread/block assignment, expanded hardware specifications and baseline reproduction details, including checkpoint provenance, OmniQuant training settings and GPTQ activation ordering. These materially improve implementation documentation. The earlier worked bits-per-weight calculation, inference implementation discussion and artifact-license list disappear.

R1.justification: Research positioning shifts substantially toward framework compatibility and quantization resource costs. v2 adds substantive discussion of AQLM, Student Float, LLM-QAT, Marlin, LUT-GEMM and llama.cpp, and expands discussion of QUIP#. Earlier FlashAttention, KV-cache quantization and NOMAD-attention references disappear.

P1.justification: The title, abstract and introduction are extensively rewritten around versatility and scalability. Background and methodology are reorganized by grid type, experiments emphasize accuracy and quantization resources, and BERT evaluation and error-accumulation discussion move into the appendices.

P2.justification: The paper changes from two-column to single-column formatting. Separate motivation figures become a combined histogram/grid comparison, loss-error plots gain affine/non-uniform traces, and tables are reorganized by grid type. Perplexity and BERT tables move to appendices; MT-Bench graphics and resource tables are added.

improvement.justification: v2's controlled initialization/kernel studies, broader task evaluation and baseline reproduction details make the method better supported and easier to assess. However, inconsistent GPTQ averaging in Tables 1/8 inflates headline comparisons, and unexplained duplicated 7B/13B rows weaken confidence in some added results. Removal of the limitations discussion and direct inference measurements also reduces transparency. These drawbacks substantially temper the benefits, leaving a limited net quality improvement.
